question: Which layer holds an agent scope open, and does a CPUQuota on the agent slice actually close the leak?

live_state.ppid1_residents_are: legitimate infra daemons (guardrails_srv, privacy-aware) in this agent's own scope, not leaked test guests
live_state.note: acute 2026-08-04 burst (17 procs / 2 dead scopes / ~752 CPU-hours) is CLEARED; structural gap persists independently

slice_enforcement_measured.consequence: cpu absent from subtree_control => per-agent scopes expose NO cpu.max file; memory.max and pids.max ARE present per-scope

leak_mechanism_results.conclusion: CPUQuota THROTTLES exactly as configured but NEVER REAPS; cgroup.kill reaps atomically. A quota alone converts an unbounded core burn into a bounded burn that still runs forever and still pins the scope.

layer_confirmation.claim: leaked spinners are bash, not hermit
layer_confirmation.source_evidence: hermit b64d893a hermit-cli/tests/cli.rs: spawns via Command::output() (:36-38) / .spawn() (:43-48); grep -c kill_on_drop == 0; no process_group, no timeout, no subtree containment
layer_confirmation.implication: the guest subtree is one layer BELOW hermit and reparents to init when the supervisor dies; a PATH shim named 'hermit' wraps the wrong layer AND misses explicit-path invocations

fix.a_throttle: systemd drop-in on 3pai_sandbox.slice (CPUQuota/MemoryMax/TasksMax) — necessary, INSUFFICIENT (does not reap)
fix.b_reap: periodic sweeper writing cgroup.kill to any 3pai_sandbox.slice/*.scope whose owning run-p<PID> is dead AND which is non-empty — the part a quota cannot do
fix.c_adoption: route cargo test / test_harness.sh / ad-hoc runs through the existing verified whole-tree box (teardown.py::reap + scheduler.py); complementary to (b)
fix.owner_constraint: a scope-level reaper was previously forbidden as 'a second reaper'; the two-signal condition (owner dead AND non-empty) cannot touch a live agent's work, which was the original objection — evidence to revisit, not to overrule
